message.subject: Reducing support tickets on outdoor graphics
message.body:
Hi [Name],

I've been following Canon's recent Colorado M-series updates and noticed the emphasis on weather-resistant vehicle wrap applications.

We work with technical teams at other large-format printer manufacturers who were getting recurring support tickets about UV fading and cracking on outdoor prints. They started recommending our PVF protective films as overlaminates, and it's significantly reduced those complaints—especially on vehicle wraps and architectural graphics where customers expect multi-year performance.

Given Canon's focus on outdoor durability, would it be helpful if I sent over some technical specs and application guidance your team could reference during customer consultations?

Best,
[Your name]

personalization_used.hook: Technical Services likely handles recurring support tickets about print longevity on vehicle wraps and architectural graphics where customers expect multi-year performance based on Canon's marketing claims
personalization_used.value_prop_emphasized: UV protection and durability to reduce support ticket volume related to outdoor performance failures
